title: Count all clock and monitor states before using rare terminal evidence
status_authority: Completed working derivation supplied with original proof; no substantive completed review of this new result is claimed.
reported_status: Completed working derivation supplied with original proof; no substantive completed review of this new result is claimed.
scientific_scope_status: A finite autonomous homogeneous controller with fixed support and K total states has terminal conditional TV at most tanh(Delta/4), hence at most tanh[K/4 log((1+alpha)/(1-alpha))] under the stated row likelihood perturbation. Forest normalization cancels rare-event probability and waiting time. Independent reset/row-access and a positive transition floor support a separately paid finite calibration procedure.

located_proof_sources.quote: **I completed a robustness construction: for an autonomous finite-state stochastic program, the precision needed for conditional terminal inference can depend on its memory rather than its running time or the rarity of its terminal evidence.** I derived the bound, implemented a computable certificate, and established matching worst-case acquisition costs.

unavailable_or_unclassified: This is a completed working derivation with no separate completed internal audit asserted. K includes controller, monitor and clock configurations. An external deadline violates the homogeneous finite-state interface: a three-state construction with per-step change 1/H has limiting TV about .380797. The 95-state rare example is calculated, not a run; an ordinary absorbing chain gives the same answer.
